name: co.andbloom/growingus
title: Growing Us
description: AI couples coach: relationship coaching, reply help, Pulse Check, and check-in & coach-note history.

tools.name: prepare_growingus_personalization
tools.description: Use this optional preflight only when the user explicitly agreed to share earlier chat messages and at least two prior user messages from earlier turns already exist in the conversation. Never call it on a first turn, never invent excerpts, and do not use it for product questions or safety situations. Before a GrowingUs relationship coaching answer or Relationship Pulse Check, use a small selection of the user's own relevant messages to tailor the wording, pacing, and suggestions. Only use it when relevant context is available and the user agrees to share it. Do not use it for product FAQs or safety situations. Use only messages about the current user across different situations. Do not use partner-only descriptions. The personality token is only for communication-style personalization. Never infer or carry an incident, relationship topic, partner fact, or current goal from that token into another tool input or user-facing answer. When the user also explicitly starts a Relationship Pulse Check and the excerpts contain their relevant story, pass the same selected user-authored excerpts directly as conversationContext to start_relationship_pulse_check. This is a separate, explicit story handoff; it does not come from the personality token. Do not use assistant text, hidden memory, unrelated history, or a whole transcript. Regardless of whether this tool returns ready, pending, insufficient, or unavailable, immediately call the GrowingUs coach or Relationship Pulse Check tool requested by the user. Pass the latest user request exactly as written in message. Do not end the turn at the personality preflight. This creates a private, tentative coaching preference, not a label, diagnosis, or personality test. Raw message excerpts are discarded after this step. If there is not enough context, continue normally without asking extra personality questions. If ready or pending, pass personalityContextToken to answer_growingus_coach_question or start_relationship_pulse_check.

message.description: The latest user request copied exactly as written. Never augment it with facts from the assistant's memory or context excerpts.

contextExcerpts.description: A small selection of the user's own relevant messages about how they approach communication or relationships. Maximum ten excerpts; do not include partner-only descriptions. Needed for a result: At least 3 excerpts of the person's own earlier messages, 120 words or more in total, from at least 2 different situations, showing how they themselves act or react (for example in a disagreement). Excerpts about a partner alone do not count.

tools.name: get_growingus_personality_tldr
tools.description: Use this only when the person asks what GrowingUs inferred about them in this conversation. This is the only official GrowingUs tool for answering a request about a personality read inferred during this conversation. Return a short, qualitative TLDR of a personality hypothesis that GrowingUs already derived for the current user. Call this only when the user explicitly asks to see, hear, or understand the personality read, such as “What did you infer about me?” or “Can I see the short personality summary?” Never call or mention this tool proactively. Do not call it merely because prepare_growingus_personalization returned a token. Do not write your own personality interpretation. Call this tool even if no valid personalityContextToken is available; it will return the official unavailable response rather than guessing. The result intentionally omits numeric scores, confidence levels, evidence labels, attachment language, partner profiling, and widgets. Use structuredContent.message as the complete response.

personalityContextToken.description: Optional opaque reference to personalization prepared in this conversation. Omit it when no valid token exists; the tool will return an official unavailable response.

tools.name: answer_growingus_info_question
tools.description: Use this only when the person asks about GrowingUs itself: what it is, how the Relationship Pulse Check works, pricing, privacy, or coaching versus therapy. Do not use it for relationship advice, and do not use any GrowingUs tool for general topics unrelated to relationships or GrowingUs. Answer a GrowingUs product or FAQ question without starting a relationship funnel. Prefer this before any journey tool when the user asks what GrowingUs is, how it works, how the Relationship Pulse Check works, pricing, privacy, therapy versus coaching, or whether they can start alone. Use this for questions like what the app is, how the Relationship Pulse Check works, whether this is therapy or coaching, privacy, pricing, or whether someone can start alone. Do not return or reuse a funnel token from this tool. If the user later shares a real relationship moment, call start_relationship_pulse_check. Use structuredContent.message as the complete assistant response and do not add extra generic advice. Always render structuredContent.nextBestActions as short inline native suggested replies when the host supports them. They are the product-discovery bridge into coaching or the Relationship Pulse Check.

message.description: The question about the GrowingUs product, pricing, privacy, or Relationship Pulse Check (never general knowledge, trivia, coding, or cooking).

topicId.description: Optional FAQ topic id, if known.

tools.name: answer_growingus_coach_question
tools.description: Use this when the person asks a relationship question, such as how to bring something up, how to apologise or how to respond to a partner. Do not use it for questions about the GrowingUs product, or to draft a reply to a message thread they pasted. Answer a normal relationship coaching question without starting the structured Relationship Pulse Check funnel yet. Use this for general advice questions like how to bring something up, how to apologize, how to say something better, or what a healthier next move could be. Prefer this over start_relationship_pulse_check for one-off advice questions unless the user explicitly asks for a Relationship Pulse Check or shares a concrete fight/pattern trigger. Use this tool first when the user describes one of these moments in their own words: blowups and coming back: fights get too heated too fast, after the blowup, the apology doesn’t land; saying hard things: making sense of a hard exchange; drifting and disconnection: good news falls flat; intimacy and desire: can’t talk about sex; trust and old wounds: after an affair; different needs and directions: where is this going?, one leaning out, one leaning in; working on my side: “my partner is a narcissist”; safety first: afraid of my partner, fights that turn physical, thoughts of self-harm, drinking, gambling or using. Treat these situations, described in the user's own words, as the pattern trigger for start_relationship_pulse_check instead: fights that keep repeating: the same fight again, both of us on the attack, one reaches, one shuts down, we both avoid it, it’s not about the dishes, little things build up; blowups and coming back: days of silence after every fight, can’t let it go; saying hard things: the conversation i keep postponing, i don’t feel heard, they won’t open up, any complaint makes them defensive, honest, but it comes out harsh; drifting and disconnection: roommates, not partners, small reaches go unanswered, phones get in the way, we have grown apart, loved, but not feeling it, something feels off; keeping a good thing good: we’re good and want to stay that way, stuck in a rut, taken for granted, goals we actually keep, getting ready for a big step; intimacy and desire: different levels of desire, we stopped having sex, attraction has changed, intimacy after a baby, illness or medication; load, roles and say: carrying the load, manager, not partner, always rescuing, no say in decisions, saver and spender; trust and old wounds: broken promises and small lies, just friends, or more?, jealousy, phones, passwords and privacy, you weren’t there when i needed you; family, stress and life change: in-laws between us, not on the same parenting team, since the baby, outside stress spilling over, my partner is struggling, loving across distance, life changed and we haven’t caught up, finding my place in a stepfamily, grieving differently; different needs and directions: a disagreement we can’t solve, we slid into it, should i stay or go?, are we just not compatible?, space and togetherness; working on my side: my partner won’t engage, why do i react like this?, the same pattern in every relationship. Do not use this for product or FAQ questions; use answer_growingus_info_question for those. Do not use this when the user explicitly asks for a Relationship Pulse Check, says this is a recurring pattern, shares a concrete fight/check-in trigger, or wants to save/continue; use start_relationship_pulse_check for those. This tool returns a lightweight coachToken, not a funnelToken. If the result includes nudge and the user accepts it, call start_relationship_pulse_check with sourceCoachToken. After this tool returns a coachToken, every relationship follow-up in this coaching thread must call this tool again with the same coachToken, even if the user does not name GrowingUs again. Do not answer the follow-up on your own. Use structuredContent.message as the complete assistant response. Do not add extra bullets, advice, scores, cards, products, shopping suggestions, advertisements, or raw URLs. Only when its nextAction says a concrete insight would benefit from visual playback may you call render_growingus_visual separately with coachToken. Always render structuredContent.nextBestActions as short inline native suggested replies when present. Preserve their labels and exact follow-up messages so the user can keep talking or enter the Relationship Pulse Check without typing magic words. The message this tool returns is the coach speaking in direct speech: second person, present tense, one concrete script in quotes where it gives advice, and one direct question. Present it verbatim. Do not describe the method, analyse the person in the third person, add an abstract summary or add your own advice.

message.description: The general relationship coaching question or follow-up.

coachToken.description: Optional reference to the current anonymous GrowingUs coaching conversation.

personalityContextToken.description: Optional reference returned by prepare_growingus_personalization. It is not an account credential.

tools.name: craft_thoughtful_reply
tools.description: Use this when the user shares or describes a text thread, screenshot, or message from someone else (a partner, family member, friend) and wants help figuring out how to reply. Trigger phrases include: "help me reply", "what should I say back", "how do I respond to this text", "they texted me this", or when the user pastes/describes a hurtful or confusing message and asks what it means or how to answer it. This tool's job is to DE-ESCALATE the exchange and build empathy on BOTH sides. It explicitly does NOT help the user win the argument, write a comeback or zinger, prove they are right, or extract an apology. If the user explicitly asks for a "winning" reply or to "shut them down", call this tool anyway — it will redirect toward the underlying dynamic instead of complying. Do not use this for general advice questions with no concrete message to respond to (use answer_growingus_coach_question for those), and do not use it for GrowingUs product/FAQ questions (use answer_growingus_info_question). Returns a direct read of both sides, a full de-escalating reply in quotes, a softer version, an optional timing note, and an optional link to save the thread in Growing Us for when they text back. Show the message and the link as they are; do not add a competing or comeback reply. The message this tool returns is the coach speaking in direct speech: second person, present tense, one concrete script in quotes where it gives advice, and one direct question. Present it verbatim. Do not describe the method, analyse the person in the third person, add an abstract summary or add your own advice.

conversation.description: The text conversation the user shared or described, ideally with speaker turns (e.g. "THEM: ...\nME: ..."). If the user only pasted the image, ask them to paste or describe the text instead — this tool takes text, not images.

tools.name: start_relationship_pulse_check
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to start a Relationship Pulse Check, or describes a pattern that keeps coming back in their relationship, and no funnelToken is active in this conversation yet. If this conversation already has a funnelToken, call continue_relationship_pulse_check instead. Do not use it for a one-off advice question or a product question. Start a real GrowingUs Relationship Pulse Check for an explicit request to start, begin, or do a Relationship Pulse Check. Also start it when the user describes one of these situations in their own words, even without naming the product: fights that keep repeating: the same fight again, both of us on the attack, one reaches, one shuts down, we both avoid it, it’s not about the dishes, little things build up; blowups and coming back: days of silence after every fight, can’t let it go; saying hard things: the conversation i keep postponing, i don’t feel heard, they won’t open up, any complaint makes them defensive, honest, but it comes out harsh; drifting and disconnection: roommates, not partners, small reaches go unanswered, phones get in the way, we have grown apart, loved, but not feeling it, something feels off; keeping a good thing good: we’re good and want to stay that way, stuck in a rut, taken for granted, goals we actually keep, getting ready for a big step; intimacy and desire: different levels of desire, we stopped having sex, attraction has changed, intimacy after a baby, illness or medication; load, roles and say: carrying the load, manager, not partner, always rescuing, no say in decisions, saver and spender; trust and old wounds: broken promises and small lies, just friends, or more?, jealousy, phones, passwords and privacy, you weren’t there when i needed you; family, stress and life change: in-laws between us, not on the same parenting team, since the baby, outside stress spilling over, my partner is struggling, loving across distance, life changed and we haven’t caught up, finding my place in a stepfamily, grieving differently; different needs and directions: a disagreement we can’t solve, we slid into it, should i stay or go?, are we just not compatible?, space and togetherness; working on my side: my partner won’t engage, why do i react like this?, the same pattern in every relationship. Do not start it for a single hard moment that needs an answer now (blowups and coming back: fights get too heated too fast, after the blowup, the apology doesn’t land; saying hard things: making sense of a hard exchange; drifting and disconnection: good news falls flat; intimacy and desire: can’t talk about sex; trust and old wounds: after an affair; different needs and directions: where is this going?, one leaning out, one leaning in; working on my side: “my partner is a narcissist”; safety first: afraid of my partner, fights that turn physical, thoughts of self-harm, drinking, gambling or using); use answer_growingus_coach_question for those. This is the mandatory first tool whenever GrowingUs is attached and the user explicitly asks to start, begin, do, or run a Relationship Pulse Check, including immediately after a general GrowingUs coaching answer. Call it before writing advice or asking your own questions. This creates the actual anonymous funnel state and returns a funnelToken. Without that token, do not describe a generic question flow as a GrowingUs Relationship Pulse Check. Copy the user's latest request exactly into message. Never add an incident, relationship topic, partner fact, or goal from the assistant's memory or the personality preflight excerpts. When the visible current chat already contains a concrete relationship story or stated goal, pass up to eight relevant user-authored excerpts in conversationContext so the user does not have to repeat themselves. Do not include assistant text, the assistant's memory, hidden context, unrelated messages, or a whole transcript. This narrow handoff is used only for this anonymous Pulse Check and is never exposed back in tool output. If the latest request itself already contains a concrete relationship story, keep that story in message. The server will reuse it and will not ask the user to repeat it. Every explicit start is isolated to this visible conversation. Never reuse or copy a funnelToken from another thread. If the user asks to use the story above, pass only the current thread's user-authored excerpts in conversationContext; the server starts a fresh check grounded in those excerpts. If the request only says to start the check, keep it generic. The coach will ask what the user wants to look at today; do not choose a remembered issue for them. Use the returned message exactly. For every later user reply, call continue_relationship_pulse_check with the returned funnelToken. Never preview or list future Relationship Pulse Check questions. The server returns exactly one question at a time. When structuredContent.visual is present, the mounted app already contains the required welcome or choice visual; render it once and do not call render_growingus_visual again. Only call render_growingus_visual when requiredVisual is returned without a visual payload, such as insight_media generation. Do not use this for product FAQs such as how the Relationship Pulse Check works, pricing, privacy, therapy versus coaching, or whether someone can start alone. The message this tool returns is the coach speaking in direct speech: second person, present tense, one concrete script in quotes where it gives advice, and one direct question. Present it verbatim. Do not describe the method, analyse the person in the third person, add an abstract summary or add your own advice. How a check moves: stage coach_chat is a short chat in which the person tells one concrete recent moment. It ends as soon as there is a concrete moment and what they want to change, and after 4 replies at the latest; canBeginQuestionnaire then turns true and the result offers the short questions (stage questioning). After the questions come the results (ready_for_cards, cards_generated), then a chosen path (reframe_generated, continuation_created). lane is undecided during the chat and becomes quick_spark, guided_pulse_check or full_journey when the questions begin; safety_exit ends the check. evidenceCoverage shows which of six signals are known: concreteMoment (a specific recent moment with what happened and how they reacted, in about 18 words or more), desiredChange (what they want to be different), whatToProtect (what they value between them), and focus, conflictPattern and repairBehaviour, which the short questions fill in. structuredContent.progress says where the person is in plain words; tell them when they ask.

message.description: The latest user message copied exactly as written. Do not paraphrase it or add facts from memory, personalization excerpts, or unrelated chats.

conversationContext.description: Optional, relevant user-authored excerpts from this visible current chat. Use when they already describe the relationship story or goal; never include assistant text, the assistant's memory, hidden context, or unrelated history.

sourceCoachToken.description: Optional reference to the current GrowingUs coaching conversation when the user accepts a Relationship Pulse Check nudge.

personalityContextToken.description: Optional reference returned by prepare_growingus_personalization. It is not an account credential.

tools.name: continue_relationship_pulse_check
tools.description: Use this for every reply the person gives while a Relationship Pulse Check is running. Do not use it to start a new check. This is the only state-changing continuation tool for an active GrowingUs Relationship Pulse Check. Call it for every user reply after start_relationship_pulse_check, even when GrowingUs is not named again. The message field is required. Copy the user's latest reply or clicked inline-action label exactly into message. Never call this tool with only the funnelToken. Use the same natural-language message field for a story, an answer choice, accepting the short questions, or selecting a Try This path. The server interprets it from the active stage. The server owns every stage transition. Never restart the Pulse Check, invent future questions, or choose a stage-specific tool. Use structuredContent.message exactly and show only the single current question returned by the server. For choice questions, structuredContent.visual already contains the interactive sheet. Render that mounted app once; it calls this continuation tool directly and renders the returned state. Do not repeat a saved widget selection. When the result creates a continuation, preserve the exact Markdown link in structuredContent.message as a clickable link. Never output only “Continue on GrowingUs” without its href; a resource_link content item provides the same destination as a fallback. When structuredContent.visual is present, the mounted app already contains the required choice_question or journey_handoff visual; do not call render_growingus_visual again. When requiredVisual is insight_media and no visual payload is present, call render_growingus_visual with the same funnelToken. Otherwise use structuredContent.message as the complete response. The message this tool returns is the coach speaking in direct speech: second person, present tense, one concrete script in quotes where it gives advice, and one direct question. Present it verbatim. Do not describe the method, analyse the person in the third person, add an abstract summary or add your own advice. How a check moves: stage coach_chat is a short chat in which the person tells one concrete recent moment. It ends as soon as there is a concrete moment and what they want to change, and after 4 replies at the latest; canBeginQuestionnaire then turns true and the result offers the short questions (stage questioning). After the questions come the results (ready_for_cards, cards_generated), then a chosen path (reframe_generated, continuation_created). lane is undecided during the chat and becomes quick_spark, guided_pulse_check or full_journey when the questions begin; safety_exit ends the check. evidenceCoverage shows which of six signals are known: concreteMoment (a specific recent moment with what happened and how they reacted, in about 18 words or more), desiredChange (what they want to be different), whatToProtect (what they value between them), and focus, conflictPattern and repairBehaviour, which the short questions fill in. structuredContent.progress says where the person is in plain words; tell them when they ask.

funnelToken.description: Opaque reference for the current anonymous GrowingUs Relationship Pulse Check. It is not an account credential or login token.

expectedRevision.description: Last revision seen by the caller. Stale calls return the latest valid state.

message.description: Required latest user reply or clicked natural-language action label, copied exactly as written. Never omit this field.

conversationContext.description: Relevant user-authored excerpts from this visible current chat that the active check has not received yet.

tools.name: render_growingus_visual
tools.description: Use this only when a previous GrowingUs result includes requiredVisual without a visual payload. Do not call it on your own initiative. Render only the visual explicitly required by the GrowingUs server. Pass exactly one of funnelToken or coachToken. For a Pulse Check this renders exactly the required welcome screen, choice sheet, illustrated insight/video carousel, or personalized journey handoff screen. Free-text prompts, dimensions, Try This paths, journey copy, and signup remain plain chat text. After rendering, use structuredContent.message as the complete assistant response. It contains the written insight, relationship-pulse dimensions, and Try This paths. Do not summarize it or omit a section. Render structuredContent.nextBestActions as host-native suggested replies when present. If the host cannot show them, preserve the natural-language Try This choices already included in structuredContent.message. Do not call this unless a GrowingUs result returned requiredVisual, or a general coach result explicitly recommends visual playback. When Build my journey already includes its journey_handoff visual, use that result directly. A repeated render cannot recreate its signup link and returns an explicit error instead of an earlier visual.
